chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who begins his obligatory salat (prayer), then remembers that he did not recite the iqamah. He said: If he remembers that he did not recite the iqamah before he has begun reciting, then let him send salutations upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, then recite the iqamah and perform the salat (prayer). But if he remembers after he has recited part of the surah, then let him continue with his salat (prayer).

The proper way regarding these reports as well is that we interpret them as indicating a kind of recommendation, just as we interpreted the first report in that manner, so that the reports do not conflict; and that is indicated by what follows.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation, meaning the act is preferable rather than obligatory
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارُ: the reports, referring to the transmitted hadith narrations
key_terms.بَعْضَ السُّورَةِ: part of the surah, indicating a point in the prayer after recitation has begun
key_terms.صَلَاتَهُ الْمَكْتُوبَةَ: his obligatory salat (prayer), meaning the prescribed daily prayer
key_terms.فَلْيُسَلِّمْ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ: let him send salutations upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم before restarting properly
key_terms.يَسْتَفْتِحُ: begins or opens, referring to commencing the prayer
key_terms.يُقِمْ: to recite the iqamah, the call immediately preceding congregational or individual prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets the iqamah after starting the obligatory salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of one who begins the obligatory salat (prayer) and then remembers that he omitted the iqamah. If he remembers before recitation, he may recite the iqamah and begin properly; but if he remembers after reciting part of the surah, he should continue the salat (prayer). The closing statement indicates that such reports are understood in the sense of recommendation rather than obligation, to reconcile the narrations.
